Re: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Reference Number: POC-8E43F25837-44913
Date of Notice: August 11, 2026
Requested Service: Hip arthroscopy, CPT 29914
Treating Surgeon: Okafor, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To the Appeals Review Team:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 29914 (arthroscopy, hip, surgical; with femoroplasty) dated August 11, 2026. The stated reason for denial was that "the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity." I am submitting this appeal within the 180-day deadline stated in the notice (due by February 7, 2027), and I am providing the additional clinical detail below to address the stated gap.

**Policy criteria at issue**

My understanding is that Cigna applies its cobranded EviCore musculoskeletal guideline, CMM-314: Hip Surgery – Arthroscopic and Open Procedures, to determine medical necessity for hip arthroscopy for femoroacetabular impingement (FAI). I was able to obtain and directly quote the criteria language from the version of this guideline effective August 1, 2024. Cigna's own published policy-update log states that CMM-314 had "no clinically impactful changes" as of its most recent confirmed update prior to this denial, and the version whose cover page states it is effective March 7, 2026 restates the same definitions and general-guideline framework verbatim in the portions I was able to review. I could not independently retrieve the full FAI-specific criteria section of the March 7, 2026 version, so I am relying on and quoting the text of the 2024 version below. If the plan applied different or updated wording in my case, I ask that Cigna identify the specific version and section used and reconcile it with the clinical evidence below.

That guideline states:

"Arthroscopic or open hip surgery for femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) is considered medically necessary when ALL of the following criteria have been met: Imaging shows BOTH of the following findings: FAI confirmation with X-ray, MRI, or CT showing ANY of the following findings: Alpha angle greater than 50 degrees; Pistol-grip deformity; Decrease of femoral head-neck offset; Acetabular retroversion (i.e., crossover sign, ischial spine sign); Coxa profunda — Presence of Tönnis grade 0-1 osteoarthritis."

"Physical exam demonstrates BOTH of the following findings: Positive anterior impingement sign (i.e., groin-dominant hip pain with forced hip flexion, adduction, and internal rotation); Limited passive hip internal rotation."

"Symptoms include groin-dominant hip pain that is worsened by flexion (e.g., squatting or prolonged sitting) and significantly limits activities."

"Unresponsive to at least three (3) months of provider-directed non-surgical treatment which must include the following (unless contraindicated): An image-guided intra-articular hip injection with local anesthetic (with or without corticosteroid) to which there was a positive response (i.e., any degree of pain reduction achieved within 2 weeks after the injection)."

**How my clinical record satisfies each criterion**

1. Imaging findings: My MRI arthrogram of the hip, performed June 8, 2026, documents an anterosuperior labral tear with cam-type femoroacetabular impingement and an alpha angle of 68 degrees, which exceeds the "greater than 50 degrees" threshold in the guideline. The same study documents preserved joint space with a Tönnis grade of 0. Together, this record satisfies both imaging elements quoted above.

2. Physical exam: My exam findings include positive provocative testing on the affected hip and range of motion limited by pain. [If available, please have Dr. Okafor's office confirm and specifically document that the provocative test performed was the anterior impingement sign (hip flexion, adduction, and internal rotation) and that internal rotation specifically was limited on passive exam, since the guideline requires both of these specific findings and the summary I have does not break this out by named test.]

3. Symptoms: For 24 months I have had progressive hip pain, described clinically as sharp anterior groin pain with sitting and pivoting. I am currently unable to run or squat. This matches the guideline's description of "groin-dominant hip pain that is worsened by flexion (e.g., squatting or prolonged sitting) and significantly limits activities."

4. Non-surgical treatment: I have completed the following conservative treatment, all of which is documented in my chart:
 - NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief;
 - A corticosteroid injection on May 23, 2026, which gave only 3 weeks of partial relief;
 - Supervised physical therapy focused on core and hip stabilization with activity modification, 18 visits over 8 weeks (May 26, 2026 – July 21, 2026), documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
This treatment course spans well over three months when the NSAID trial, injection, and physical therapy are considered together, and it did not produce durable relief. [Please have the ordering physician's office confirm and document that the May 23, 2026 corticosteroid injection was image-guided and included a local anesthetic component, and the degree/duration of pain reduction achieved within two weeks of that injection, since the guideline specifically requires an image-guided intra-articular injection with local anesthetic and my current summary does not confirm the imaging-guidance and anesthetic details.]

I also note, for completeness, that I have no active infection, no untreated substance use disorder, a BMI of 29, and I am a non-smoker — none of which are identified in my records as contraindications to surgery.

**Request**

Based on the imaging, symptom, and conservative-treatment documentation above — most of which was already in the prior authorization packet — I ask that Cigna reverse the denial of CPT 29914 and approve the requested hip arthroscopy. If any specific element above (the named provocative test, the internal-rotation finding, or the imaging-guidance/anesthetic detail of the corticosteroid injection) is what led the reviewer to characterize the file as "incomplete," I ask that this be identified specifically so that Dr. Okafor's office can supply a supplemental letter addressing that exact point before the appeal deadline.

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and advise if any additional forms are required. If this internal appeal is denied, I intend to pursue an independent external review through the Illinois Department of Insurance, as permitted under Illinois law.

Sincerely,

Casey Hayes
Member ID: W225149976
